# Community Rule Column 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QS (Cave 1), Col. 6 | **Condition:** complete

---

**6:1** Furthermore, no one should bring an accusation against a fellow member before the full assembly without first confronting him privately with witnesses present.

**6:2** These are the guidelines for how they live together. Whenever members are together, the younger must defer to the older in matters of work and finances.

**6:3** They must eat together, pray together, and deliberate together. Wherever ten members of

**6:4** the community council are gathered, a priest must always be present among them. Each person sits according to his rank before the priest, and in that same order

**6:5** they are consulted about every issue. When the table is set for a meal, or when the fresh wine is prepared

**6:6** for drinking, the priest must be the first to reach out his hand and pronounce the blessing over the first portion of bread and wine.

**6:7** Wherever the group of ten meets, someone must always be engaged in studying the Torah, day

**6:8** and night without interruption, with members taking turns to relieve one another. The full assembly must maintain a nightly vigil during a third of every night throughout

**6:9** the year, reading from Scripture, studying its meaning, and offering prayers of blessing together.

**6:10** This is how the assembly sessions are to be conducted. Each person takes his assigned seat: the priests sit first, then the elders, then all

**6:11** the remaining members, each in his proper place. They follow this same order when consulted about any ruling, any deliberation, or any matter

**6:12** brought before the assembly, so that each person can contribute his insight to the community council.

**6:13** No one may interrupt another person while he is still speaking, and no one may speak until his brother has finished. Nor may anyone speak

**6:14** ahead of someone who outranks him. Each person speaks only when called upon, in proper order. During sessions of

**6:15** the full assembly, no one may say a word without the assembly's permission. Now, regarding

**6:16** the Guardian who presides over the assembly — if anyone has something to contribute to the assembly's discussion

**6:17** but does not hold the position of the one authorized to put questions before the community council, that person must rise to his feet

**6:18** and say: "I have something to bring before the assembly." If they give him permission, he may speak.

**6:19** When any Israelite volunteers to join the community council,

**6:20** the Guardian who leads the assembly must interview him about his understanding and his conduct. If he shows readiness for the community's way of life,

**6:21** the Guardian shall bring him into the covenant commitment to live by the truth and abandon all wrongdoing. He shall then teach him all the community's rules.

**6:22** Later, when the candidate comes to stand before the full assembly, all the members shall be asked about his case.

**6:23** Based on the outcome of the assembly's vote, he will either be accepted or turned away. If he is accepted into the community council,

**6:24** he must not share in the assembly's consecrated food until they have thoroughly evaluated his character and behavior — and not until he has spent a full year in this status.

**6:25** He is also excluded from sharing in the community's common funds during this time.

**6:26** After completing one year in the community, the full assembly reviews his case — examining his understanding and his faithfulness to the Torah. If the assembly votes to advance him into the community council, with the approval of the priests and the majority of the covenant members,

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering of 1QS Column 6. "Full assembly" and "assembly" render ha-rabbim (the Many). "Guardian" renders mebaqqer (Instructor/Overseer). "Consecrated food" interprets tohorat (purity) in its practical communal context. "Fresh wine" for tirosh. Hierarchical seating order (priests, elders, members) conveyed for modern readers.*
